scenes.text: It's July 1920, and the line outside your office goes around the block.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: School Street in downtown Boston, July 1920: granite office buildings, a long sidewalk outside a doorway, 1920 Ford cars, summer sun

scenes.text: Thousands of people are pushing to hand you their savings.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: School Street in downtown Boston, July 1920: granite office buildings, a long sidewalk outside a doorway, 1920 Ford cars, summer sun

scenes.text: You promise them fifty percent profit in forty-five days.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: School Street in downtown Boston, July 1920: granite office buildings, a long sidewalk outside a doorway, 1920 Ford cars, summer sun

scenes.text: A bank pays them about five percent a year.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And it works. Every old investor gets paid, right on time.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small busy investment office in Boston, 1920: wooden counter with brass teller grilles, stacks of cash and paper notes on desks, filing cabinets, ceiling fans

scenes.text: Here's the secret: there is no business. There never was.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small busy investment office in Boston, 1920: wooden counter with brass teller grilles, stacks of cash and paper notes on desks, filing cabinets, ceiling fans

scenes.text: Thirty years from now, you'll die in a charity ward in Brazil with seventy-five dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: charity hospital ward in Rio de Janeiro, 1940s: rows of white iron beds, tall shuttered windows, ceiling fans, tropical light

scenes.text: And your name will become the word for this kind of fraud.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By the end, you'll know the one money rule that got you here, and whether it still works today.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But to get here, we have to go back. It's 1882, and you're born in Lugo, Italy.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: Your name is Carlo Ponzi. Keep count of two things: the money, and the jail cells.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: Your family isn't rich, but your mother has big dreams for you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: She tells everyone her son will be a gentleman.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: You work as a postal clerk, which matters later. Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: In Lugo, the post office handles money orders and stamps, and you learn exactly how they work.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: Then you get into the University of Rome.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: Rome is full of rich young men from famous families.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: Your new friends are rich. You are not.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: So you spend like them anyway: cafes, theaters, nice clothes.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You never finish a degree. You finish your money instead.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your family decides America might fix you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: You've been the best-dressed man in town on borrowed money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: In America, everyone says the streets are paved with gold.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small town square in Lugo, northern Italy, 1890s: arcaded medieval buildings, stone fortress walls, cobbles, bicycles, warm afternoon light

scenes.text: In November 1903, you sail into Boston on a steamer.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your family gave you two hundred dollars for the trip.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Card players on the ship took most of it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You step off with two dollars and fifty cents.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: I landed in this country with $2.50 in cash and $1 million in hopes.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: I landed in this country with $2.50 in cash and $1 million in hopes.

scenes.text: The streets are not paved with gold. They're barely paved.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You wash dishes in a restaurant and sleep on its floor.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your English gets good. So does your charm.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: They promote you to waiter. That's your first big break.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Then they catch you short-changing customers and stealing.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You move from city to city along the East Coast, always a little behind on rent.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: They fire you. For the next four years, job after job goes the same way.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Grocery clerk. Factory hand. Fired, fired, fired.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Somewhere in all this, you learn your first real lesson.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: People trust a man who looks rich more than a man who is rich.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1907, you move to Montreal and get a job in a bank.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: It's a tiny bank for Italian immigrants, run by Luigi Zarossi.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: Zarossi pays six percent interest. Other banks pay half that.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: Customers love him. Deposits pour in.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: You move into the Zarossi family home, and you help run the place.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: You're the assistant teller, so you see the books.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: And the books are a disaster.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: The bank's loans have gone bad. There's no profit to pay that six percent.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: So Zarossi pays old depositors with new depositors' money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: You watch this closely. Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: The new money stops. The bank collapses.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: Zarossi runs off to Mexico with a large part of the money.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: tiny immigrant bank in Montreal, 1907: narrow storefront office, one teller window, ledgers, Italian flag pennant, snow outside the window

scenes.text: You're broke again, in a strange city, in winter.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You've learned how a bank can look healthy while it is completely empty.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So you walk into an office and write yourself a check.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Four hundred and twenty-three dollars, signed with someone else's name.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The police find you within days.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You get three years in a Quebec prison.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: You write to your mother in Italy with exciting news.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: You tell her you've taken a job as special assistant to a prison warden.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

paper.text: DEAR MOTHER: I AM NOW SPECIAL ASSISTANT TO THE WARDEN

scenes.text: Which is one way to describe being an inmate.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: You're out after twenty months, in 1911.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: Then you help smuggle five Italian immigrants across the border into the United States.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That's another two years, this time in Atlanta's federal prison.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: You become the warden's translator, reading Italian prisoners' mail.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: And you meet a fellow inmate: Charles Morse, a famous Wall Street banker.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: Morse had a fifteen-year sentence for bank fraud.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: He eats soap shavings to make himself look terribly sick.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Doctors are fooled. The President pardons him, and he walks out.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Prison, it turns out, is a pretty good business school.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: You learn your second lesson: rich men don't stay in prison long.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: By 1917 you're back in Boston, and you meet Rose Gnecco.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: She's a stenographer: a typist who takes notes in shorthand.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You marry her in 1918. She has no idea about the prisons.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You take over her father's grocery business.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You run it into the ground in months.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Then you try a business catalog for export merchants. Nobody buys ads.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But one day in August 1919, a letter comes from Spain.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Boston post office counter, 1919: brass mail slots, stamp windows, scales, wanted posters board, wooden floor

scenes.text: Inside is a small slip of paper: an International Reply Coupon.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Boston post office counter, 1919: brass mail slots, stamp windows, scales, wanted posters board, wooden floor

scenes.text: You can trade it at any post office for a stamp to send a reply.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Boston post office counter, 1919: brass mail slots, stamp windows, scales, wanted posters board, wooden floor

scenes.text: Remember being a postal clerk in Italy? This is where it pays off.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Boston post office counter, 1919: brass mail slots, stamp windows, scales, wanted posters board, wooden floor

scenes.text: The coupon prices were set before the war, and the Italian lira has crashed since.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Boston post office counter, 1919: brass mail slots, stamp windows, scales, wanted posters board, wooden floor

scenes.text: So coupons are cheap to buy in Italy, and they buy more stamps in America.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Boston post office counter, 1919: brass mail slots, stamp windows, scales, wanted posters board, wooden floor

scenes.text: On paper, every dollar of coupons turns into several.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Boston post office counter, 1919: brass mail slots, stamp windows, scales, wanted posters board, wooden floor

scenes.text: There's just one problem. You'd need millions of coupons, and you can't sell stamps for cash.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Boston post office counter, 1919: brass mail slots, stamp windows, scales, wanted posters board, wooden floor

scenes.text: You decide that's a detail.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Boston post office counter, 1919: brass mail slots, stamp windows, scales, wanted posters board, wooden floor

scenes.text: On December 26th, 1919, you open the Securities Exchange Company.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You promise fifty percent in forty-five days. Or double your money in ninety.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The first few investors are friends and neighbors.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: When their forty-five days are up, you pay them. In full.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: With money from the next investors.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember Zarossi? This is exactly what he did. Just bigger.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Let's be clear about how this works, because it's named after you.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: empty corner bakery, 1920: bare wooden shelves, glass display case with no bread, flour sacks, a chalk price board, morning light

scenes.text: Imagine a bakery that sells no bread.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: empty corner bakery, 1920: bare wooden shelves, glass display case with no bread, flour sacks, a chalk price board, morning light

scenes.text: It borrows ten dollars from Anna and promises her fifteen next month.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: empty corner bakery, 1920: bare wooden shelves, glass display case with no bread, flour sacks, a chalk price board, morning light

scenes.text: Next month, it borrows twenty from Ben, and pays Anna her fifteen.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: empty corner bakery, 1920: bare wooden shelves, glass display case with no bread, flour sacks, a chalk price board, morning light

scenes.text: Anna tells everyone how great the bakery is.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: empty corner bakery, 1920: bare wooden shelves, glass display case with no bread, flour sacks, a chalk price board, morning light

scenes.text: Now it needs Ben's thirty, so it needs even more new customers.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: empty corner bakery, 1920: bare wooden shelves, glass display case with no bread, flour sacks, a chalk price board, morning light

scenes.text: It only survives while new money grows faster than the promises.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: empty corner bakery, 1920: bare wooden shelves, glass display case with no bread, flour sacks, a chalk price board, morning light

scenes.text: Every month, the bakery must find more new customers than the month before.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: empty corner bakery, 1920: bare wooden shelves, glass display case with no bread, flour sacks, a chalk price board, morning light

scenes.text: The day new money slows down, the whole bakery collapses at once.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: empty corner bakery, 1920: bare wooden shelves, glass display case with no bread, flour sacks, a chalk price board, morning light

scenes.text: Someone is always last in line. They lose everything.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: empty corner bakery, 1920: bare wooden shelves, glass display case with no bread, flour sacks, a chalk price board, morning light

scenes.text: You weren't the first to do this. In 1899, William Miller in Brooklyn promised ten percent a week.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The internet calls you the inventor of the Ponzi scheme. You didn't invent it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You just made it famous. Very, very famous.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In February 1920, investors hand you about five thousand dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In March, it's thirty thousand.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You hire agents and pay them ten percent for every dollar they bring in.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small busy investment office in Boston, 1920: wooden counter with brass teller grilles, stacks of cash and paper notes on desks, filing cabinets, ceiling fans

scenes.text: In May, it's four hundred and twenty thousand.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small busy investment office in Boston, 1920: wooden counter with brass teller grilles, stacks of cash and paper notes on desks, filing cabinets, ceiling fans

scenes.text: Police officers invest. Bank clerks invest. Your own lawyers invest.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: People mortgage their houses to buy your paper notes.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By July, money arrives faster than your clerks can count it.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small busy investment office in Boston, 1920: wooden counter with brass teller grilles, stacks of cash and paper notes on desks, filing cabinets, ceiling fans

scenes.text: Your agents work on commission, so they sign up their own families first.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small busy investment office in Boston, 1920: wooden counter with brass teller grilles, stacks of cash and paper notes on desks, filing cabinets, ceiling fans

scenes.text: They stuff cash into closets, drawers and wastebaskets.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small busy investment office in Boston, 1920: wooden counter with brass teller grilles, stacks of cash and paper notes on desks, filing cabinets, ceiling fans

scenes.text: You start dressing like the gentleman your mother always promised.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small busy investment office in Boston, 1920: wooden counter with brass teller grilles, stacks of cash and paper notes on desks, filing cabinets, ceiling fans

scenes.text: You buy control of a real bank: the Hanover Trust Company.

scenes.text: In 1920, air conditioning is basically science fiction.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: large colonial-revival mansion in Lexington, Massachusetts, 1920: white columns, wide lawn, gravel drive, a shiny 1920 limousine

scenes.text: You bring your mother over from Italy in a first-class cabin.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: large colonial-revival mansion in Lexington, Massachusetts, 1920: white columns, wide lawn, gravel drive, a shiny 1920 limousine

scenes.text: Remember? She always said you'd be a gentleman.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: large colonial-revival mansion in Lexington, Massachusetts, 1920: white columns, wide lawn, gravel drive, a shiny 1920 limousine

scenes.text: And you look exactly like one. Remember that lesson about looking rich?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: large colonial-revival mansion in Lexington, Massachusetts, 1920: white columns, wide lawn, gravel drive, a shiny 1920 limousine

scenes.text: You buy maybe a few dollars of actual coupons, as a test.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small busy investment office in Boston, 1920: wooden counter with brass teller grilles, stacks of cash and paper notes on desks, filing cabinets, ceiling fans

scenes.text: The newspaper that ends you is just weeks away.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small busy investment office in Boston, 1920: wooden counter with brass teller grilles, stacks of cash and paper notes on desks, filing cabinets, ceiling fans

scenes.text: In July, a furniture dealer sues you for a million dollars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Then the Boston Post publishes a front-page story asking how you do it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: BOSTON POST: QUESTIONS ON PONZI PROFITS

scenes.text: A crowd rushes your office to pull their money out.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: School Street in downtown Boston, July 1920: granite office buildings, a long sidewalk outside a doorway, 1920 Ford cars, summer sun

scenes.text: And you pay every single one of them.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: School Street in downtown Boston, July 1920: granite office buildings, a long sidewalk outside a doorway, 1920 Ford cars, summer sun

scenes.text: You even hand out coffee and doughnuts to the people in line.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: School Street in downtown Boston, July 1920: granite office buildings, a long sidewalk outside a doorway, 1920 Ford cars, summer sun

scenes.text: Someone in the crowd shouts that you're the greatest Italian of them all.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: School Street in downtown Boston, July 1920: granite office buildings, a long sidewalk outside a doorway, 1920 Ford cars, summer sun

scenes.text: You play modest. Columbus discovered America. Marconi discovered the wireless.

scenes.bgIdea: School Street in downtown Boston, July 1920: granite office buildings, a long sidewalk outside a doorway, 1920 Ford cars, summer sun

quote.text: Columbus discovered America. Marconi discovered the wireless.

scenes.text: Another voice shouts back: But you discovered money!
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The run stops. The crowds come back to invest more.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: School Street in downtown Boston, July 1920: granite office buildings, a long sidewalk outside a doorway, 1920 Ford cars, summer sun

scenes.text: Then a financial journalist named Clarence Barron does some math.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: To cover your notes, you'd need about one hundred sixty million coupons.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: There are only about twenty-seven thousand in circulation.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Barron asks one more question: why don't you put your own money in your own scheme?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And the post office confirms nobody is buying coupons in bulk.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You've hired a publicity man, William McMasters, to polish your image.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He reads your books instead.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: On August 2nd, he tells the Boston Post you're hopelessly insolvent.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The man you paid to make you look good just made you look like a fraud.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Insolvent means you owe more than you have. Millions more.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A second run starts. This time the money doesn't last.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Thousands of people now want their money back at the same time.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Then the Post digs up a photo from Montreal.

scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The Hanover Trust and five other banks fail with you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Investors have lost about twenty million dollars.

scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Out on bail, you head to Florida, where everyone is buying land.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Florida swampland lot for sale, 1925: palmettos, standing water, wooden survey stakes, a hand-painted blank sign, hot sun

scenes.text: Florida land prices are rising so fast that people buy lots they have never seen.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Florida swampland lot for sale, 1925: palmettos, standing water, wooden survey stakes, a hand-painted blank sign, hot sun

scenes.text: You sell lots in a new development and promise two hundred percent in sixty days.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Florida swampland lot for sale, 1925: palmettos, standing water, wooden survey stakes, a hand-painted blank sign, hot sun

scenes.text: Many of the lots are underwater. Literally: it's a swamp.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Florida swampland lot for sale, 1925: palmettos, standing water, wooden survey stakes, a hand-painted blank sign, hot sun

scenes.text: Investors get a piece of paper, and you get their cash. Sound familiar?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Florida swampland lot for sale, 1925: palmettos, standing water, wooden survey stakes, a hand-painted blank sign, hot sun

scenes.text: Florida convicts you too. You skip bail, shave your head, and try to sail to Italy as a sailor.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: They catch you at the dock in New Orleans.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Back to Massachusetts. Seven more years.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: early 1900s prison cell block: iron bars, stone walls, narrow cot, tin cup, a high barred window with grey light

scenes.text: Remember Morse, who ate soap to get out? It doesn't work for you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1934, America deports you to Italy. You never became a citizen.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By now you've spent about fourteen years of your life behind bars.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Rose stays in Boston. She divorces you a few years later.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You write a book about yourself, The Rise of Mister Ponzi.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Italy gives you a job with its national airline, in Rio de Janeiro.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: charity hospital ward in Rio de Janeiro, 1940s: rows of white iron beds, tall shuttered windows, ceiling fans, tropical light

scenes.text: Then the war starts, Brazil sides against Italy, and the job disappears.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You teach English. You translate letters. You get sick.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A stroke leaves you half paralyzed and nearly blind.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: charity hospital ward in Rio de Janeiro, 1940s: rows of white iron beds, tall shuttered windows, ceiling fans, tropical light

scenes.text: Late in life, a reporter asks if you have regrets. You don't, really.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: charity hospital ward in Rio de Janeiro, 1940s: rows of white iron beds, tall shuttered windows, ceiling fans, tropical light

scenes.text: Even if they never got anything for it, it was cheap at that price.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: charity hospital ward in Rio de Janeiro, 1940s: rows of white iron beds, tall shuttered windows, ceiling fans, tropical light

quote.text: Even if they never got anything for it, it was cheap at that price.

scenes.text: I had given them the best show since the landing of the Pilgrims!
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: charity hospital ward in Rio de Janeiro, 1940s: rows of white iron beds, tall shuttered windows, ceiling fans, tropical light

quote.text: I had given them the best show... since the landing of the Pilgrims!

scenes.text: On January 18th, 1949, you die in a charity hospital in Rio.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: charity hospital ward in Rio de Janeiro, 1940s: rows of white iron beds, tall shuttered windows, ceiling fans, tropical light

scenes.text: You leave seventy-five dollars, enough for a funeral.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: charity hospital ward in Rio de Janeiro, 1940s: rows of white iron beds, tall shuttered windows, ceiling fans, tropical light

scenes.text: The internet says you hid millions somewhere. Nobody ever found a cent.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: charity hospital ward in Rio de Janeiro, 1940s: rows of white iron beds, tall shuttered windows, ceiling fans, tropical light

scenes.text: Your scheme ran for about eight months. Your name has lasted for more than a hundred years.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: charity hospital ward in Rio de Janeiro, 1940s: rows of white iron beds, tall shuttered windows, ceiling fans, tropical light

scenes.text: So how did a man with two dollars and fifty cents get Boston to hand him millions?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: large colonial-revival mansion in Lexington, Massachusetts, 1920: white columns, wide lawn, gravel drive, a shiny 1920 limousine

scenes.text: He paid the first people on time. And they did his selling for him.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: large colonial-revival mansion in Lexington, Massachusetts, 1920: white columns, wide lawn, gravel drive, a shiny 1920 limousine

scenes.text: Nobody asked where the profit came from, because the checks cleared.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: large colonial-revival mansion in Lexington, Massachusetts, 1920: white columns, wide lawn, gravel drive, a shiny 1920 limousine

scenes.text: That brings us to today's money rule.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: MONEY RULE: FIND WHERE PROFIT COMES FROM

scenes.text: If you can't see where the profit comes from, assume it comes from you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Say a website promises you three percent a month, guaranteed.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That sounds small. It's over forty percent a year.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A US savings account paid about four or five percent a year in 2024.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: A gap that big needs a business that big. Ask to see it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Real profit comes from a product, rent, interest, or work that someone can check.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Payments from you to old investors look exactly the same, until the day they stop.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And the rule isn't perfect. Your early investors asked questions too, and got paid.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Ask for audited accounts: reports checked by an outside accountant.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: If the answer is a secret system, that is your answer.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Getting paid once proves nothing. Seeing the business proves something.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You promised them the best show in Boston. They just had to buy the tickets.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: large colonial-revival mansion in Lexington, Massachusetts, 1920: white columns, wide lawn, gravel drive, a shiny 1920 limousine

Your Life as the Man Who Became a Word for Fraud

meta.thumbnail: A crowded 1920 Boston street with a long line of people waving cash at an office door, paper notes flying; text: '50% IN 45 DAYS'
meta.description:
It's July 1920. Thousands of people line up to hand you their savings, and you pay every one of them on time.
There is no business. There never was. This is the life of Charles Ponzi.

A comedic dramatization of documented history.
General education only, not financial advice.

Sources:
- Charles Ponzi, Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Ponzi
- Mitchell Zuckoff, Ponzi's Scheme: The True Story of a Financial Legend (2005)
- Charles Ponzi, The Rise of Mr. Ponzi (1935)
- Ponzi scheme, Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponzi_scheme
factCheck: Born March 3, 1882, in Lugo, Italy; worked as a postal clerk, attended the University of Rome without graduating, spent beyond his means (Wikipedia).
Arrived in Boston November 1903 aboard the SS Vancouver with $2.50 after gambling away most of his savings on the voyage; the $200 figure is from his own account and DISPUTED.
Dishwasher who slept on the restaurant floor, promoted to waiter, fired for short-changing customers and theft (Wikipedia).

1907 Montreal: assistant teller at Banco Zarossi, run by Luigi 'Louis' Zarossi, paying 6% interest (double the going rate) from new deposits; bank failed and Zarossi fled to Mexico with much of the money (Wikipedia).

Forged a check for $423.58 from the Canadian Warehousing Company; three years at St. Vincent de Paul Penitentiary, released after about 20 months (Wikipedia). Letter to his mother calling himself special assistant to the warden (Wikipedia).

1911: two years in Atlanta federal prison for smuggling five Italian immigrants across the Canadian border; translator for the warden; met Charles W. Morse, who ate soap shavings to appear ill and won early release (Wikipedia). Morse was sentenced to 15 years in 1908 and pardoned by President Taft in 1912.
1918 married Rose Maria Gnecco, a stenographer; ran her father's grocery business badly; export trade catalog failed (Wikipedia).

August 1919: letter from a Spanish company containing an International Reply Coupon; post-war inflation made IRCs bought in Italy worth more in US stamps; IRCs could not be resold for cash (Wikipedia).

Securities Exchange Company founded Dec 26, 1919; 50% in 45 days or 100% in 90 days; Feb 1920 about $5,000, March $30,000, May $420,000; by July millions, about $250,000 a day (Wikipedia). Agents paid commissions (10% is commonly cited).
William F. '520 Percent' Miller, Brooklyn 1899, promised 10% a week (Wikipedia, Ponzi scheme article).

Bought controlling interest in Hanover Trust Company; Lexington mansion with air conditioning and a heated swimming pool; brought his mother from Italy in a first-class stateroom (Wikipedia). 'Twenty-room' is approximate.
July 1920: furniture dealer Joseph Daniels sued for $1 million; July 26 Boston Post article questioned the business; Ponzi paid out the run and served coffee and doughnuts (Wikipedia).
Clarence Barron: 160 million coupons needed, about 27,000 in circulation (Wikipedia). Post office said IRCs were not being bought in quantity.

Publicist William McMasters; Aug 2, 1920 Boston Post article declared Ponzi hopelessly insolvent; Post then revealed his Montreal conviction; Ponzi surrendered Aug 12, 1920 (Wikipedia). Running money totals on the counter are rough estimates.
Hanover Trust and five other banks failed; investors lost about $20 million; ~$300M today using CPI x16 (1920 to 2026, approx). Boston Post won the 1921 Pulitzer Prize for Public Service (Wikipedia).

Pleaded guilty to mail fraud, five years federal prison; then state larceny charges; out on bail, 1925 Florida land scheme (Charpon Land Syndicate) promising 200% in 60 days, land partly swamp; convicted in Florida, fled, shaved head, caught in New Orleans 1926 trying to sail to Italy as a crew member; seven more years in Massachusetts (Wikipedia).

Deported to Italy in 1934 (never naturalized); Rose divorced him in 1937; wrote The Rise of Mr. Ponzi; worked for Ala Littoria airline in Brazil from 1939 until Brazil joined the Allies in 1942 (Wikipedia).
Stroke, partial paralysis, nearly blind; died January 18, 1949 in a charity hospital in Rio de Janeiro, leaving $75 for burial (Wikipedia).

Quotes from Wikipedia: '$2.50 in cash and $1 million in hopes' and 'best show... since the landing of the Pilgrims' (late-life interview). Columbus/Marconi exchange with the crowd from Zuckoff via Wikipedia.
2024 US savings accounts: high-yield accounts paid about 4-5% APY (FDIC national rate was lower). 3% a month compounds to about 42.6% a year.
